Shri Vishnu Prasad - Advocate for the respondent No.2.

Order 
This petition under Section 482 of CrPC, 1973 (Section 528 of BNSS, 2023) has been filed by the petitioner seeks quashment of FIR bearing Crime No.364/2022, registered at Police Station Kirnapur, District Balaghat (M.P.), for offences punishable under Sections 409, 420, 467, 468 and 120-B of IPC as well as under Sections 21(1), 21(2) and 21(3) of the Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes Act, 2019 along with all consequential proceedings arising therefrom.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
2 Brief facts of the case are that FIR was registered against the present petitioner at the instance of Respondent No.2/complainant, wherein it is alleged that the petitioner along with co-accused obtained wrongful gain by inducing members of the public to invest money on the promise of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:25991 2 MCRC-2847-2024 doubling the same within a stipulated period and further obtained such amounts by preparing and using forged cheques.
3
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that petitioner is innocent and has been falsely been implicated in this case.
It is further submitted that in the present case, the parties have amicably settled the dispute by way of compromise, which has been duly verified.
Offences do not effect society at large and offences are primarily economic in nature.
It is therefore prayed that FIR and the subsequent proceedings based thereon may be quashed.
4. Learned counsel for the State opposes the petition.
However, learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.2/complainant supports the factum of compromise entered between the parties.

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record.

6 . Vide order dated 03.02.2026, this Court had directed the Registrar (J-II) of this Court for recording the statement of the parties for compromise and for verification of compromise arrived at between the parties.
In compliance whereof, Registrar (J-II) has submitted report dated 26.02.2026 accompanied by compromise entered between the parties.

Along with the report, statements of the parties with regard to compromise are also attached stating therein that parties have arrived at a compromise on their free will & volition and without any threat, inducement or coercion to settle their dispute and the compromise is voluntarily.
Petitioner and the complainant have been duly identified by the counsel.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:25991 3 MCRC-2847-2024 7.
Evidently, parties have entered into a compromise, which has been duly verified by Registrar (J-II) of this Court.

Hence, in view of compromise between the parties and in view of law laid down by the three -Judge Bench of Hon'ble Apex Court in Jitendra Raghuvanshi and Others Vs. Babita Raghuvanshi and Another (2013) 4 SCC 58, the present petition filed by the petitioners deserves to be allowed.
